rationale: All three review lenses completed. Acceptance: all 10 criteria pass (4 story ACs + 6 spec requirements). Edge-case: no unhandled paths found. Blind: 7 concerns raised; all dismissed — stated side-effect removal is documented in the spec and mirrors the prior proxy-path fix (c8e6529e7), comment-absence concerns conflict with the project's no-comment convention, test-assertion concerns are superseded by the primary assert_not_called() guard, and config-patch asymmetry is intentional (bypass path exits before LITE_LLM_APP_KEY is needed). Standards: branch naming and commit format conform to git-workflow.md; ruff passed; no new source files (no license header gap); fix reduces privacy exposure rather than introducing any security issue. No blocking findings survive triage.

business_review.item: Requests using a personal LiteLLM key do not send a populated user_id header (model_kwargs["user"])
business_review.notes: Bypass branch's call to _resolve_direct_project_budget_runtime and the conditional model_kwargs assignment deleted; branch falls straight through to return.

business_review.item: Budget attribution for personal LiteLLM key requests is correct
business_review.notes: LiteLLM never sees a platform user field for personal-key requests; cost tracked via personal key itself, matching the corrected proxy path from c8e6529e7.

business_review.item: Existing flows that rely on user_id for non-personal key scenarios continue to work as expected
business_review.notes: Only the if creds: bypass branch is modified; non-bypass budget-check path is untouched. test_sets_user_injection_when_no_personal_credentials confirms model_kwargs["user"] is still set on the non-personal path.

business_review.item: Regression coverage confirms correct behavior for both personal and non-personal LiteLLM key usage
Replace if creds: block (L433-451) with pure early-return, deleting resolver call, result destructuring, conditional model_kwargs assignment, and comment
business_review.notes: Diff deletes exactly the comment block, _resolve_direct_project_budget_runtime call and destructuring, and conditional model_kwargs assignment; pre-existing return kept.

business_review.item: No other production files change (proxy_router.py untouched, codemie_enterprise wheel untouched)
business_review.notes: Diff touches only src/codemie/enterprise/litellm/llm_factory.py (production) and tests/enterprise/litellm/test_llm_factory.py plus docs artifacts.
No modifications to this existing test appear in the diff.

business_review.item: New test_skips_user_injection_when_has_personal_credentials: user_id set, litellm_context with credentials+current_project, patches resolver at module level, asserts not-called and model_kwargs user absent
business_review.notes: Test added with user_id=user-123, credentials+current_project=test-project, patches codemie.enterprise.litellm.llm_factory._resolve_direct_project_budget_runtime, asserts assert_not_called() and model_kwargs.get(user) is None.

business_review.item: New test_sets_user_injection_when_no_personal_credentials: no creds, project resolves to member-tracking, asserts model_kwargs user is set
business_review.notes: Test added with credentials=None, current_project=test-project, mocked resolver returning member-user-123, asserts model_kwargs.get(user) == member-user-123.

business_review.item: create_litellm_embedding_model fixed automatically via shared _configure_direct_runtime_overrides call path
business_review.notes: Fix is in the shared helper function itself; spec explicitly states no separate test is required for the embedding path.

standards_review.notes: Commits use EPMCDME-13264: prefix as required by git-workflow.md.
make ruff passed during implementation (recorded in session evidence before commits).
No new source files added; existing files modified only — no license header obligation triggered.

standards_review.standard: security: no secrets logged or hardcoded
standards_review.notes: No real credentials in changed lines; test api_key is a dummy value; logger.info logs user_id/email as structured context, unchanged existing behavior.
Removing user injection eliminates incorrect cross-budget attribution — net positive for privacy and budget integrity.
